per_case.answer: Chickenpox is a common and extremely infectious childhood disease that also affects adults on occasion. It is also known as varicella [1].

Antibiotics are ineffective against chickenpox because it is a viral disease [1]. Additionally, it is stated that "Antibiotics are ineffective against viruses, though antiviral drugs exist for some viruses, including chickenpox" [2].
A single attack of chickenpox almost always confers lifelong immunity against the disease [1].

Cirrhosis is a chronic, degenerative disease in which normal liver cells are damaged and are then replaced by scar tissue [1]. It changes the structure of the liver and the blood vessels that nourish it, reducing the liver's ability to manufacture proteins and process hormones, nutrients, medications, and poisons [1].

Conjunctivitis is the inflammation of the conjunctiva, a thin, delicate membrane that covers the eyeball and lines the eyelid [1]. It is also described as an inflammation or redness of the lining of the white part of the eye and the underside of the eyelid [3]. Conjunctivitis is an extremely common eye problem [2].

Conjunctivitis can be caused by a viral infection, such as a cold, acute respiratory infection, or diseases like measles, herpes simplex, or herpes zoster [1]. It can also be caused by hazards like wind, smoke, dust, and allergic reactions caused by pollen, dust, or grass [2]. Additionally, exposure to sun lamps or electrical arcs used during welding, and problems with inadequate drainage of the tear ducts, can cause conjunctivitis [2].

Dementia is defined as a loss of mental ability severe enough to interfere with normal activities of daily living, lasting more than six months, not present since birth, and not associated with a loss or alteration of consciousness [3].

Cancer is caused by substances that induce mutations, such as carcinogens, and is often associated with prolonged exposure [1]. Additionally, cancer cells have been altered such that they are more likely to develop and grow uncontrollably [1].
No, cancer is not a single disease. According to the CONTEXT, cancer is a "large group of almost one hundred diseases" [1].

Celiac disease is a disease of the digestive system that damages the small intestine and interferes with the absorption of nutrients from food [1]. It is classified as an "autoimmune" disorder and may also be called sprue, nontropical sprue, gluten sensitive enteropathy, celiac sprue, and adult celiac disease [2]. The disease occurs when the body reacts abnormally to gluten, a protein found in wheat, rye, barley, and possibly oats, leading to an inflammatory response in the small intestine and impaired ability to absorb nutrients [3].

Croup is a common childhood ailment that arises from a viral infection of the larynx (voice box) and is associated with mild upper respiratory symptoms such as a runny nose and cough [2]. The typical root cause of the infection is Parainfluenza viruses, but influenza (flu) and cold viruses may sometimes be responsible [1]. The hallmark sign of croup is a harsh, barking cough, which may be preceded by one to three days of symptoms that resemble a slight cold [3].
The most striking feature of diphtheria is the formation of a grayish membrane covering the tonsils and upper part of the throat [1].
Diphtheria usually involves the nose, throat, and air passages [1]. It specifically affects the pharynx, which connects the mouth and nasal passages with the voice box [3].

Cystic fibrosis (CF) is an inherited disease that affects the lungs, digestive system, sweat glands, and male fertility [1]. It affects the body's ability to move salt and water in and out of cells, causing the lungs and pancreas to secrete thick mucus [1].

Colic is persistent, unexplained crying in a healthy baby between two weeks and five months of age [1]. It is not a disease and affects 10–20% of all infants [1]. Symptoms of colic usually appear when a baby is 14–21 days old, reach a crescendo at the age of three months, and disappear within the next eight weeks [1].
Constipation is defined as an acute or chronic condition in which bowel movements occur less often than usual or consist of hard, dry stools that are painful or difficult to pass [1, 2, 3].
An adult who has not had a bowel movement in three days is considered constipated [1].

Depressive disorders are mental illnesses characterized by a profound and persistent feeling of sadness or despair and/or a loss of interest in things that were once pleasurable [2]. Disturbance in sleep, appetite, and mental processes are a common accompaniment [2]. Changes in the levels of certain neurotransmitters, such as serotonin, norepinephrine, and dopamine, are thought to be related to depressive disorders [3].

Carpal tunnel syndrome is a disorder caused by compression at the wrist of the median nerve supplying the hand, causing numbness and tingling [1]. It is characterized by the hand feeling as if it has "gone to sleep" when the median nerve is compressed [2].

A concussion is a trauma-induced change in mental status, with confusion and amnesia, and with or without a brief loss of consciousness [1]. It occurs when the head hits or is hit by an object, or when the brain is jarred against the skull, with sufficient force to cause temporary loss of function in the higher centers of the brain [1].

A cough is a forceful release of air from the lungs [4]. It serves a protective function by clearing the respiratory system of irritants and secretions [1], and aids the body in clearing the respiratory system of infective agents and irritants [2].

Dehydration is the loss of water and salts essential for normal body function [1]. It occurs when the body loses more fluid than it takes in [3]. This condition can result from various factors, including illness, hot and dry climates, not drinking enough water, and overuse of diuretics or other medications that increase urination [3].

Contact dermatitis is the name for any skin inflammation that occurs when the skin's surface comes in contact with a substance originating outside the body [1]. It is the most common skin condition requiring medical attention and the foremost source of work-related disease [1]. Contact dermatitis is an allergic reaction to something that irritates the skin and is manifested by one or more lines of red, swollen, blistered skin that may itch or burn [2].
There are two kinds of contact dermatitis: irritant and allergic. This is stated in passage [1] as "There are two kinds of contact dermatitis, irritant and allergic."
Down syndrome is the most common cause of mental retardation and malformation in a newborn [2]. It occurs because of the presence of an extra chromosome [2].

Dyslexia is a learning disability characterized by problems in reading, spelling, writing, speaking, or listening [2]. It is a condition where people have trouble learning early reading skills, problems hearing individual sounds in words, analyzing whole words in parts, and blending sounds into words [4]. Dyslexia is not a disease, but rather a different way of learning [1].

Endometriosis is a condition in which bits of the tissue similar to the lining of the uterus (endometrium) grow in other parts of the body [1]. This tissue builds up and sheds in response to monthly hormonal changes and may form ovarian cysts (endometriomas) [2]. It is a progressive condition that usually advances slowly, over the course of many years [2].
Botulism antitoxin is given to adults if it can be administered within 72 hours after symptoms are first observed [2]. If given later, it provides no benefit.
When breathing is impaired in botulism, patients are put on a mechanical ventilator to assist their breathing [1].
Folic acid deficiency results in anemia characterized by red blood cells that are large in size but few in number [2]. This type of anemia is one of the most common of all vitamin deficiencies [2].
The chickenpox rash typically lasts about a week [1].
Applying wet compresses or bathing the child in cool or lukewarm water once a day can help the itch [1].
According to the CONTEXT, in cirrhosis, damaged liver cells are replaced by scar tissue [1].

Cold sores usually appear on or around the lips [1]. They most often occur on the lips, which distinguishes them from canker sores [1]. In 95% of the patients with cold sores, the blisters occur at the outer edge of the lips, which is called the "vermilion border" [3].
According to the CONTEXT, dementia is not associated with a loss or alteration of consciousness [2].
Celiac disease interferes with the absorption of nutrients from food [1] and also causes an impaired ability to absorb nutrients from foods [2].

Croup is usually not serious, and most children recover within a few days [1]. In fact, it is described as a "temporary condition" and children typically recover completely within three to six days [3].
The name 'cystic fibrosis' derives from the fibrous scar tissue that develops in the pancreas, one of the principal organs affected by the disease [1].

Infant colic typically occurs between two weeks and five months of age [1]. Symptoms usually appear when a baby is 14–21 days old, reach a crescendo at the age of three months, and disappear within the next eight weeks [1].

Yes, diphtheria can be fatal. According to passage [1], the mortality rate varies from 1.5–25% in countries that do not have routine immunization against this infection. Passage [2] also states that obstruction of the airway may result in respiratory compromise and death.

The median nerve is compressed in carpal tunnel syndrome. This is stated in passage [2]: "Carpal tunnel syndrome is a disorder caused by compression at the wrist of the median nerve supplying the hand, causing numbness and tingling."

According to the CONTEXT, symptoms that accompany a concussion include:

* confusion [1]
* dizziness [1]
* vacant stare or confused expression [1]
* incoherent or incomprehensible speech [1]
* incoordination or weakness [1]
* amnesia for the events immediately preceding the blow [1]
* nausea or vomiting [1]
* double vision [1]
* ringing in the ears [1]
* headache [3]
* disorientation as to time, date, or place [3]
* confusion [3]
* anxiety [4]
* depression [4]
* sleep disturbances [4]
* light and noise intolerance [4]

Note that some of these symptoms may be present in other conditions as well, but they are listed as possible symptoms of a concussion in the provided CONTEXT.

Coughing is considered protective because it clears the respiratory system of irritants and secretions [1]. This helps the body to expel infective agents and irritants, aiding in the protection of the respiratory system [2]. Additionally, coughing helps break up secretions in the lungs so that the mucus can be suctioned out or expectorated [3].

The body loses more fluid than it takes in during dehydration [1]. This condition can result from various factors, including not drinking enough water, overuse of diuretics or other medications that increase urination, and excessive urination (polyuria) [2].

Glucose cannot be absorbed into cells in diabetes mellitus because most cells are unable to transport glucose into the cell without the presence of insulin [2]. When there is not enough insulin produced or when the doorway no longer recognizes the insulin key, glucose stays in the blood rather entering the cells [4].
Down syndrome is caused by an extra copy or a rearrangement of chromosome 21 [2].

Yes, research suggests that dyslexia is often inherited. This is supported by [1] and [2], which state that the condition appears to be inherited in many cases. Additionally, [3] mentions that previous studies have pointed out linkages of potential dyslexia genes to chromosomes 1, 15, and 6, suggesting a genetic component to the condition.

The displaced tissue in endometriosis grows and sheds each month during a woman's menstrual cycle, similar to the tissue lining the uterus [1]. This process is not directly described in the provided CONTEXT, but it can be inferred from the general description of the menstrual cycle and endometrium.
Cold sores are caused by a herpes simplex virus infection [3]. The herpes simplex virus is part of the human herpes viruses family [1].
Red blood cells in folic acid deficiency anemia are large in size but few in number [1].

Yes, chickenpox is a highly infectious disease. According to [1], it is "extremely infectious" and affects both children and adults. Additionally, [3] states that by ages nine or 10, about 80-90% of American children have already been infected, indicating the high contagiousness of the disease.
Cirrhosis is a chronic, degenerative disease [1]. It gets worse over time and can become potentially life threatening [1].

According to the CONTEXT, reduced mental ability must last more than six months to be considered dementia. This is stated in passage [1] as "lasting more than six months" and also in passage [2] as "lasting six months or more."

According to the CONTEXT, the key danger described for cancer cells spreading is that if they have spread to the surrounding tissues, then, even after the malignant tumor is removed, it generally recurs [1].

Celiac disease damages the small intestine and interferes with the absorption of nutrients from food, which suggests that it affects the digestive system [1]. The inflammation and malabsorption caused by celiac disease also create wide-ranging problems in many systems of the body [2].
Cystic fibrosis affects the digestive system, sweat glands, and male fertility, besides the lungs [1]. It also affects the respiratory tract, from the nose to the lungs [2].

Colic is not a disease and is defined as persistent, unexplained crying in a healthy baby between two weeks and five months of age [1]. It affects 10–20% of all infants, which suggests that the babies experiencing colic are generally healthy [1].

Disturbance in sleep, appetite, and mental processes are common accompaniments of depressive disorders besides sadness [1]. Other symptoms include sudden loss of appetite or compulsive eating, inability to concentrate, and being isolated or withdrawn [2].

Carpal tunnel syndrome causes numbness, burning, tingling, and a prickly pin-like sensation over the palm surface of the hand, and into the thumb, forefinger, middle finger, and half of the ring finger [1]. Some individuals also notice a shooting pain which goes from the wrist up the arm, or down into the hand and fingers [1].

Yes, contact dermatitis can be triggered by substances outside the body. According to the CONTEXT, "Contact dermatitis is the name for any skin inflammation that occurs when the skin's surface comes in contact with a substance originating outside the body" [1]. Additionally, it is stated that "Thousands of natural and man-made substances can cause contact dermatitis" [1].
